identity.title: RMP-SAM: Towards Real-Time Multi-Purpose Segment Anything

problem.claim: Can one end-to-end model perform interactive, panoptic, and video instance segmentation in real time?

gap.claim: Existing foundation segmentation methods are hindered by heavy encoder-decoder designs, while real-time work often targets specific environments and overlooks cross-scenario generalization.

contributions.claim: Defines real-time multi-purpose segmentation across three sub-tasks: interactive, panoptic, and video instance segmentation.
Presents RMP-SAM, a dynamic-convolution method with an efficient encoder and decoupled adapter for prompt-driven decoding.
Explores training strategies and a new adapter design, and benchmarks extended strong baselines for multi-purpose segmentation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by targeting a single end-to-end model for multiple segmentation tasks in real time, using dynamic convolution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show RMP-SAM is effective and generalizes well on proposed benchmarks and other specific semantic tasks.
The authors report that their implementation achieves the optimal balance between accuracy and speed for these tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large foundation segmentation models support multiple tasks but their heavy frameworks impede real-time performance.
Prior real-time efforts emphasize environment-specific semantic segmentation and may overlook generalization, motivating real-time multi-purpose segmentation across three sub-tasks.
RMP-SAM uses one end-to-end model with dynamic convolution, an efficient encoder, and a decoupled prompt-driven adapter; training strategies and another adapter design support co-training.
The authors benchmark extended baselines, report effectiveness, generalization, and an accuracy-speed balance, and state that code and models will be released.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly links a multi-task setting to a single end-to-end design, then describes efficiency components and training strategies intended to satisfy real-time and co-training requirements.

lessons.interpretation: A useful paper-framing pattern is to align the task definition, architectural choices, and optimization strategy with distinct constraints.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-task system, map each stated constraint to a named design component or training decision before reporting results.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the tasks do not share representations or when separate specialized models are required by the deployment setting.

unknowns: No numerical accuracy, speed, latency, hardware, baseline, benchmark, or ablation details are provided.
The abstract does not define the real-time threshold or specify which semantic tasks and scenarios support the generalization claim.
Code and model availability is stated as future-oriented; their actual release status is unknown.
